meta.title: MWORKS AI
meta.description: Brings MWORKS into DeepSeek Harness the way the official Syslab AI and Sysplorer AI assistants do. It contributes the two official MCP servers (mcp__mworks_syslab__* for Julia execution, environment detection, help search and MATLAB-to-Julia mapping; mcp__mworks_sysplorer__* for Modelica modeling, checking, translation, simulation, results and library documentation) through the Host MCP manager, so their connection state is visible and either one can be rebuilt in place without restarting DeepSeek Harness. It also adds the official MWORKS working rules to the agent instructions, plus the recovery rule: when a MWORKS call stops answering, check the state and reconnect the server instead of retrying, which only burns another timeout. On this bundle page a Runtime environment section reports the detected Syslab and Sysplorer installations and versions, the Julia runtime, the live state of both MCP servers with a Reconnect control for one that is not connected, and the MWORKS skills this session can call. Nothing is added to the conversation. Servers start on stdio from the installed products, so Syslab must be present for the Julia tools and Sysplorer for the Modelica tools; a profile without the MCP manager gets no MWORKS MCP tools and a report saying so. The plugin only reads installation paths and version files and writes nothing into the MWORKS directories. Tool calls can run for minutes, so they use a five-minute timeout. Turning it off removes both MCP servers, the tools, the instructions and the section. It also registers the MWORKS skill bundles into the session from the copies that ship inside the MWORKS installation, so those skills load whether or not another AI client (such as OpenCode) is installed; when the skill registry already resolves them from somewhere the user configured, the plugin registers nothing and leaves that choice alone.
